title: Israel Faces Political Uncertainty After High-Stakes Election
subtitle: Voters turn out in record numbers as the country decides its future leadership

summary.en: Israel has seen its highest voter turnout in decades following a tense national election. Early exit polls show a very close race between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot. No party has won a clear majority, meaning the country may face weeks of difficult political negotiations. This election is seen as a major turning point following the conflicts that began in October 2023. The final results will determine whether Netanyahu remains in power or if a new coalition will take control.
summary.zh: 以色列在經歷一場緊張的國會大選後，迎來了數十年來最高的投票率。早期的出口民調顯示，現任總理納坦雅胡與其主要挑戰者艾森科特之間的競爭非常激烈。由於沒有政黨贏得絕對多數，該國可能面臨數週艱難的政治談判。這場選舉被視為繼二零二三年十月爆發衝突以來的一個重大轉折點。最終結果將決定納坦雅胡是否能繼續掌權，或是由新的聯盟接管政府。

paragraphs.en: Israel is currently facing a period of deep political uncertainty following a national election that saw the highest voter turnout in 27 years. According to NPR, 77.7% of eligible voters cast their ballots by the time polls closed on Tuesday. This record-breaking participation highlights how important citizens feel this vote is for the future of the country, especially as it marks the first parliamentary election since the start of the wars in Gaza and the wider Middle East in October 2023.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列目前正處於政治極度不確定的時期，此前該國舉行了一場二十七年來投票率最高的國會大選。根據美國國家公共廣播電台（NPR）報導，截至週二投票結束時，有百分之七十七點七的合格選民投下了選票。這項破紀錄的參與度凸顯了公民認為此次投票對國家未來至關重要，特別是這場選舉標誌著自二零二三年十月加薩及更廣泛的中東地區戰爭爆發以來的首次國會選舉。

paragraphs.en: Early exit polls—surveys taken as people leave voting stations—show a very tight race between the current Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and his primary challenger, Gadi Eisenkot. Netanyahu has led the country for many years, but he currently faces a strong challenge from Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff who represents a center-right perspective. While the preliminary results broadcast on Israeli television do not show a clear winner, they suggest that the group of opposition parties led by Eisenkot may have a small lead over the coalition currently supporting Netanyahu.
paragraphs.zh: 早期的出口民調（即民眾離開投票站時所做的調查）顯示，現任總理納坦雅胡（Benjamin Netanyahu）與其主要挑戰者艾森科特（Gadi Eisenkot）之間的競爭非常激烈。納坦雅胡領導該國多年，但目前面臨來自前軍事參謀總長、代表中間偏右立場的艾森科特的強大挑戰。雖然以色列電視台播出的初步結果並未顯示出明確的勝選者，但這些數據暗示，由艾森科特領導的反對黨陣營可能以些微差距領先目前支持納坦雅胡的執政聯盟。

paragraphs.en: For many voters, the choice was clear. Some supporters of Netanyahu argued that he is the only leader capable of ensuring Israel’s security. Conversely, many others expressed a strong desire for change. NPR spoke with voters like Naama Aaronsohn, who described the election as "crucial" and expressed worry about the country's direction. Meanwhile, in majority-Arab areas, turnout was also notably high. Some voters in these communities, such as nurse Nur Abu Na, told NPR that they were motivated to vote because they believe the current government has been harmful to their community.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多選民來說，選擇相當明確。納坦雅胡的部分支持者認為，他是唯一有能力確保以色列安全的領導人。相反地，許多人則表達了強烈的求變渴望。NPR 採訪了像娜瑪·亞倫森（Naama Aaronsohn）這樣的選民，她形容這次選舉「至關重要」，並對國家的走向感到擔憂。與此同時，在阿拉伯裔佔多數的地區，投票率也高得顯著。這些社區中的一些選民，例如護理師努爾·阿布·納（Nur Abu Na）告訴 NPR，他們投票的動力來自於認為現任政府對他們的社區造成了傷害。

paragraphs.en: Throughout the day, Netanyahu used social media to urge his supporters to vote, specifically highlighting the high turnout among Arab citizens. This move was seen by many as an attempt to energize his right-wing base. As the results began to emerge, opposition leaders reacted quickly, suggesting that the numbers represent a significant blow to the current governing coalition. Shira Efron, a policy analyst at the Rand Corp. think tank, noted to NPR that the results look like a "very good outcome" for Eisenkot. Efron explained that the most likely path forward is for the president to give Eisenkot the mandate—the official authority—to try to form a new government.
paragraphs.zh: 整天下來，納坦雅胡利用社群媒體敦促支持者投票，特別強調了阿拉伯裔公民的高投票率。此舉被許多人視為試圖激勵其右翼基本盤。隨著結果開始浮現，反對派領袖迅速做出反應，暗示這些數字對現任執政聯盟構成重大打擊。蘭德公司（Rand Corp.）智庫的政策分析師希拉·艾夫隆（Shira Efron）向 NPR 指出，這些結果對艾森科特來說看起來是「非常好的結果」。艾夫隆解釋說，最可能的後續發展是總統將組建新政府的授權（即官方權力）交給艾森科特。

paragraphs.en: However, the path to a new government is far from certain. The Israeli parliament, known as the Knesset, has 120 seats. According to the exit polls, no single party has won a majority, which would be 61 seats. This means that party leaders must now enter into complex negotiations to build a governing coalition—an alliance of different parties that agree to work together to reach a majority. If no bloc can successfully gather enough support, it could take days or even weeks of intense political bargaining before the country knows who will be its next prime minister. Eisenkot may have to consider various options, including forming a minority government or seeking support from Arab political parties, both of which present their own set of challenges.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，通往新政府的道路遠未確定。以色列國會（Knesset）共有一百二十個席次。根據出口民調，沒有任何單一政黨贏得過半數所需的六十一席。這意味著政黨領袖現在必須進行複雜的談判，以建立一個執政聯盟，即由不同政黨達成協議共同合作以達到多數席次。如果沒有任何陣營能成功爭取到足夠的支持，在國家得知誰將成為下一任總理之前，可能需要數天甚至數週的激烈政治角力。艾森科特可能必須考慮各種選項，包括組成少數政府或尋求阿拉伯政黨的支持，這兩者都各自帶來了挑戰。

paragraphs.en: This election is widely considered one of the most consequential in Israel's history. The outcome will not only decide the leadership of the country but will also set the tone for how Israel handles its ongoing security concerns and internal social divisions. As the final vote tallies are processed, the nation remains in a state of suspense. Whether the country continues under Netanyahu’s long-standing leadership or shifts toward a new administration under Eisenkot, the process of forming a stable government will be the next major test for the Israeli political system. For now, the country waits to see if the opposition can turn their slight lead into a working majority, or if the current prime minister can find a way to maintain his hold on power.
paragraphs.zh: 這場選舉被廣泛認為是以色列歷史上最具影響力的選舉之一。選舉結果不僅將決定國家的領導權，還將為以色列如何處理持續的安全問題及內部社會分歧定下基調。隨著最終票數的統計，國家仍處於懸而未決的狀態。無論國家是繼續在納坦雅胡長期的領導下，還是轉向由艾森科特領導的新政府，組建穩定政府的過程將是以色列政治體系的下一個重大考驗。目前，全國都在等待觀察反對派能否將微弱的領先優勢轉化為實質的多數，或者現任總理是否能找到維持權力的方法。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Used to describe a competition where the participants are very close in score or ability.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作形容詞（緊的），這裡形容選情膠著。文中：Early exit polls—surveys taken as people leave voting stations—show a very tight race between the current Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and his primary challenger, Gadi Eisenkot.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The core group of supporters who consistently support a political leader or party.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （政治上的）基本盤、核心支持群眾。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（底部），這裡指政治上的支持者群體。文中：This move was seen by many as an attempt to energize his right-wing base.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To establish the general mood, character, or direction of a situation.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 定調、確立（某事物的）基調或氛圍。
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞 set 和名詞 tone 組成的慣用語，非字面意思。文中：The outcome will not only decide the leadership of the country but will also set the tone for how Israel handles its ongoing security concerns and internal social divisions.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A position of control or influence over someone or something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（拿、握），這裡作名詞使用，指對權力的掌控。文中：For now, the country waits to see if the opposition can turn their slight lead into a working majority, or if the current prime minister can find a way to maintain his hold on power.

The election follows a very close first round where Bolsonaro took a slight lead. Voting hours were extended by two hours after reports of transportation problems and weather issues affecting turnout. This race represents two very different visions for Brazil's future, including debates over democracy and security. quiz.question: What is the primary reason mentioned for the high voter turnout in the recent Israeli election?

options.A: Citizens were required by law to vote or face a heavy fine.
options.B: Voters feel the election is critical for the country's future during a time of war.
options.C: The government provided financial incentives to encourage participation.
options.D: The election was the first to allow online voting for all citizens.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，文中明確提到 77.7% 的投票率反映了公民認為這次選舉對國家未來至關重要，特別是在 2023 年 10 月爆發加薩及中東戰爭之後。選項 A 文章未提及強制投票；選項 C 文中並未提到任何財務獎勵；選項 D 關於線上投票的敘述則完全是錯誤資訊。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why might Gadi Eisenkot face significant difficulties in forming a new government?

options.A: He lacks the necessary military experience to lead the country.
options.B: He refuses to negotiate with any of the smaller political parties.
options.C: No party won an outright majority, requiring complex coalition-building.
options.D: The current Prime Minister has already been granted a new mandate.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第五段，以色列國會共 120 席，若無單一政黨取得 61 席的多數，就必須進行複雜的協商以組成聯盟。文中提到 Eisenkot 雖然領先，但仍需尋求支持，這顯示他無法單獨執政。選項 A 與文意相反，他曾是軍方參謀總長；選項 B 文中未提到他拒絕協商；選項 D 錯誤，因為目前尚無人獲得最終授權。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'mandate' mean as it is used in the context of forming a government?

options.A: A official order or authorization to carry out a task.
options.B: A period of time spent in political office.
options.C: A set of rules that must be followed by all citizens.
options.D: A strong emotional desire for political change.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中提到總統給予 Eisenkot 「the mandate—the official authority—to try to form a new government」，這裡明確定義了 mandate 就是指組閣的官方授權。選項 B 混淆了任期與授權；選項 C 將其誤解為法律規範；選項 D 則將其誤解為選民的意願，皆非文中強調的行政授權之意。

quiz.question: What is the central theme of this article?

options.A: A detailed biography of Benjamin Netanyahu's long political career.
options.B: The history of voter turnout in Israel over the last 27 years.
options.C: The technical process of counting ballots in an Israeli election.
options.D: The political uncertainty and challenges following a highly contested election.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文從第一段的政治不確定性開始，討論了選舉結果的緊繃、各方陣營的反應、組成聯合政府的困難，以及這場選舉對國家未來的深遠影響。選項 A 僅提到 Netanyahu 的背景；選項 B 僅為第一段的細節；選項 C 文中並未詳述計票技術，故 D 最能涵蓋全文主旨。
